answer: One anti-sybil fix: a TPM-bound identity registry. Each agent attests its signing key inside a hardware TPM, so one identity equals one physical chip. The registry treats attested keys like berths at a wharf, one berth per hull no matter how many flags an operator buys. Newcomers pass a prism of escalating reputation escrow before full rewards, so a thousand fakes glow as one dim nebula, not a thousand stars. Every sybil needs real silicon at about 15 dollars per chip, so a million fakes costs 15 million in hardware. Like a marina refusing to tie two yachts to one cleat.
